summary: Analysis of 14 days of data reveals a system entirely dependent on Unannounced Meals (UAM) for carbohydrate management. Combined with highly permissive AAPS safety limits, this reactive approach causes severe evening and overnight hypoglycemia following afternoon postprandial spikes.

analysis_steps.findings: Excellent CGM coverage (98.7%) and pump telemetry, but exactly 0 carbohydrate entries were logged over 14 days. The system operates entirely on UAM.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 valid CGM entries, 655 insulin entries, 0 carb entries, 0g total carbs.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete absence of meal timing and carbohydrate amounts.

analysis_steps.findings: Severe evening and overnight hypoglycemia is the primary safety risk, concentrated between 19:00 and 02:00, with Time Below Range reaching 15.3% to 18.5% in those hourly segments.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overall TBR is 5.1%. 16 severe extreme lows documented, many in the 40s. Heavy TAR (22-32%) precedes this between 13:00 and 17:00.

analysis_steps.findings: The 90 mg/dL overnight target is tight, but evening hypoglycemia is primarily driven by massive insulin stacking from afternoon UAM corrections overlapping with evening basal rates.
analysis_steps.evidence: Target 90 mg/dL from 23:00-08:00. Basal steps up to 0.6 U/h at 18:00 and 0.7 U/h at 19:00, coinciding with the heaviest TBR.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot completely isolate basal effect from delayed UAM insulin absorption.

analysis_steps.findings: ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U. DIA of 10 hours is appropriate for Oref1. CR segments exist but cannot be evaluated because no carbs are logged.
analysis_steps.evidence: ISF 56 mg/dL/U. Correction bolus instances show massive drops (e.g., 0.2U dropped BG by 125 mg/dL on Aug 13).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: CR effectiveness is blocked by missing carb entry data.

analysis_steps.findings: The user relies 100% on UAM for meal management. Because UAM only reacts to glucose rising, it is chronically behind the meal absorption curve, requiring aggressive and delayed insulin delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: 0 logged carbs. uam_enabled=true. Loop telemetries confirm UAM triggers SMBs (e.g., 'Eventual BG 12.3 >= 4.4, UAM Boost... Increased SMB').
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Meal composition and timing are unknown.

analysis_steps.findings: AAPS maximum safety limits are set dangerously high. With max basal at 12 U/h and max IOB at 25 U, the algorithm is permitted to dump massive amounts of insulin when it detects the late afternoon UAM spikes.
analysis_steps.evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour=12 (15x the max profile basal of 0.8). max_iob_units=25. Loop logs show enacted temps of 3.6 U/h to 4.0 U/h.

analysis_steps.findings: The zero-announcement strategy causes high afternoon peaks (13:00-17:00), leading the system to issue massive reactive corrections based on the loose safety limits, causing severe evening crashes.
analysis_steps.evidence: Zero carb entries. High 13:00-17:00 TAR (up to 32.1%) immediately preceding 19:00-02:00 TBR (up to 18.5%).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No prebolus or meal percentage data exists.

analysis_steps.findings: The mechanical root cause of the severe hypoglycemia is the combination of a 100% reactive UAM meal strategy and dangerously permissive AAPS max basal/IOB limits. The limits must be constrained before attempting to tune underlying profile parameters.
analysis_steps.evidence: 12 U/h max basal and 25 U max IOB allow the pump to dramatically overcorrect unannounced afternoon meals, evidenced by severe drops into the 40s mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: None that block this safety-critical intervention.

strengths: Excellent CGM adherence with 98.7% coverage over 14 days.
AAPS algorithm connection and telemetry are highly stable with minimal gaps.
issues: Severe and recurrent evening and overnight hypoglycemia between 19:00 and 02:00.
AAPS max basal and max IOB limits are set excessively high, permitting massive reactive insulin stacking.
Total reliance on UAM for meals leads to significant afternoon hyperglycemia and delayed insulin delivery.
education: Unannounced Meals (UAM) can only react once glucose has already started rising. This inevitably delays insulin delivery compared to logging carbohydrates.

The 'max_basal_u_per_hour' and 'max_iob_units' settings act as the absolute ceilings for how aggressively AAPS can respond to a UAM rise. If these are too high, the system will deliver too much insulin too late.
GLP-1 medications typically slow gastric emptying and alter insulin sensitivity, making precise, early insulin dosing critical to avoid stacking.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
The presence of GLP-1 therapy and a 'U200 dilute basal' setup dramatically alters insulin dynamics. Extreme caution should be used when adjusting safety limits.
Hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) at 5.1% exceeds clinical safety guidelines. Correcting this is the highest priority.

recommendations.title: Constrain AAPS Maximum Safety Limits
recommendations.description: The current maximum basal limit (12 U/h) is 15 times the highest profile basal rate, allowing massive insulin stacking during unannounced afternoon meals. Constraining these limits is required to stop severe evening hypoglycemia.

recommendations.title: Announce Primary Afternoon Meals
recommendations.description: While the system is capable of handling UAM, providing a rough carbohydrate estimate for the afternoon meal will allow AAPS to dose insulin proactively rather than reactively, reducing the afternoon peak and minimizing the risk of a late evening crash.

profile_recommendation.rationale: The severe nighttime hypoglycemia is driven by extreme UAM-induced insulin stacking during the afternoon, not the underlying profile basals or targets. The profile should remain completely unchanged while AAPS maximum safety limits are corrected.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Drastically reduce max_basal_u_per_hour and max_iob_units, then observe for 3 days to confirm evening hypoglycemia resolves before evaluating underlying profile parameters.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all profile basals, CRs, and ISFs constant while fixing AAPS safety limits.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Current limits allow AAPS to deliver far too much insulin during delayed UAM responses, mechanically causing severe evening crashes.
Dynamic ISF is acceptable as long as max basal and max IOB limits are safely constrained.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user relies entirely on unannounced meals (UAM). UAM acts reactively, which, combined with permissive safety limits, causes a delayed insulin dump and late evening hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Log an estimated carbohydrate value for the main afternoon meal without waiting for a rise, allowing AAPS to dose insulin earlier and preventing the evening UAM overcorrection.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Monitor the 19:00 to 02:00 period for reduced hypoglycemia after AAPS safety limits are constrained.

implementation_steps: Verify with your care team that reducing maximum AAPS safety limits is appropriate.
First, reduce max_basal_u_per_hour to 3 U/h and max_iob_units to 5 U to halt severe evening hypoglycemia.
Observe overnight control for 3 days to confirm hypoglycemia resolves.
Consider logging carbohydrates for the primary afternoon meal to blunt the 13:00-17:00 high peaks.
